title: Ka'b ibn Malik
hook: one of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk and refused to lie (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hassan ibn Thabit, who answered the Prophet's critics in verse. Your line was: the poet's pulpit. Did your four lines reach the one they were about? Day eight hundred fifty-two.

The army has come home, and one by one, the men who stayed behind file in to explain themselves. Each one has a reason, and swears to it. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, listens, accepts what they say, and asks God to forgive them. Then it's Ka'b's turn. He's a good talker. He knows it. He could build an excuse in his sleep. And he has no excuse at all. He simply put off getting ready, day after day, until the army was gone. Today: Ka'b ibn Malik, and the story he tells against himself.
screen: `THE MEN WHO STAYED BEHIND.` → `ONE EXCUSE AFTER ANOTHER.` → `KA'B HAS NONE.`

segments.voice: Ka'b tells this himself, in a long report in Sahih al-Bukhari. Before the Tabuk expedition, he says, he had never been stronger or better off. He kept meaning to prepare, and kept not doing it. Then the army left. When the Prophet returned, Ka'b came before him, and the Prophet smiled the smile of someone who is angry. Ka'b says he knew he could talk his way out of anyone's anger. But if I lie to you today, he told the Prophet, you may be pleased with me now, and God will soon turn you against me. If I tell you the truth, you'll be angry, and I hope for God's forgiveness. I had no excuse. The Prophet said: as for this one, he has told the truth. Go, until God decides about you. Then came the hard part. People were told not to speak to Ka'b and to the two others who had owned up. Ka'b would greet the Prophet and wonder whether his lips moved to answer. His own cousin would not reply to him. A letter arrived from a foreign king inviting him to come over, and Ka'b threw it in the oven. Fifty nights, the report says, the earth felt narrow to him. Then the Qur'an spoke of the three who were left behind, and of God turning to them in mercy, in surah nine. A man climbed a hill and shouted the good news. Ka'b's conclusion is the line he chose to be remembered by. God saved me only through truthfulness, he said, and part of my repentance is to speak nothing but the truth as long as I live. Truth saved him. Not quickly. Not comfortably. But it did.
screen: `I HAD NO EXCUSE.` · `AS FOR THIS ONE, HE HAS TOLD THE TRUTH.` · `NO ONE WOULD SPEAK TO HIM.` · `GOD TURNED TO THE THREE.` · then, large: `TRUTH SAVED HIM.`

segments.voice: The practice: the truth that costs. Settle, and breathe. Is there something you've been explaining away? A late reply with a made-up reason. A mistake you let someone else carry. A small cover story. Find one. Breathe in, and say to yourself, plainly, what actually happened. No excuse attached. Breathe out, and notice how that sits in your body. Then picture saying it to the person it concerns, in one or two sentences. If you pray, you can ask God for the courage of Ka'b. The bell holds the time.
Ka'b ibn Malik. One of the three who stayed behind from Tabuk, refused to make an excuse, and was forgiven through the Qur'an. Today's word.
Your line: truth saved him. Today, tell one small truth that costs you something, with no excuse attached. Day eight hundred fifty-two.

howItsDone: Muslims tell Ka'b ibn Malik's story from his own long account in Sahih al-Bukhari, read alongside surah 9:118, as a lesson in truthfulness and repentance.

fork.setup: you are Ka'b. you missed the expedition with no excuse, and you're good with words. the Prophet is waiting. what do you say?
options: make up a good excuse, like the others.
tell him plainly: I had no excuse.
fork.reveal: Bukhari keeps his words: if I lie you may be pleased now, and God will turn you against me. I had no excuse. it cost him dearly, and it saved him.

original.note: Arabic: Ka'b, son of Malik, of Medina.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man who was punished for missing a battle.
what it means: he refused to lie his way out, waited out the silence, and was forgiven.
what a scholar hears: surah 9:118 speaks of three who were left behind until the earth felt narrow to them; Bukhari's long report is Ka'b's own telling.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4418 (Ka'b ibn Malik's account of staying behind from Tabuk)
Qur'an 9:118 (the three who were left behind)

notes: Bukhari 4418 number cited from memory; confirm. 'Fifty nights' is in that report; confirm.
The hook says only that the others gave reasons and swore to them, as in Bukhari; no number of them is given.
The 'foreign king' is the king of Ghassan; 'his cousin' is Abu Qatadah. Names left out to keep one idea; confirm.
Ka'b's closing words (saved through truthfulness; speak only the truth as long as I live) paraphrased; confirm.
